findings.claim: Kühne + Nagel International AG pleaded guilty in the US District Court for the District of Columbia to five Sherman Act counts over air freight fees and surcharges in 2002 to 2007, with an agreed criminal fine of $9,865,044. The plea agreement, signed in September 2010, was approved by the court in November 2011.

In March 2012 the European Commission fined Kuehne + Nagel €53.7 million, part of €169 million in fines on 14 forwarders for four air freight surcharge cartels run from 2002 to 2007. The General Court upheld the decision in 2016 and the Court of Justice dismissed Kuehne + Nagel's appeal in February 2018.

In April 2014 New Zealand's High Court ordered Kuehne + Nagel International AG to pay a NZ$3.1 million penalty plus costs; the company admitted taking part in a cartel that fixed surcharges on UK-to-New Zealand air freight, after losing a challenge to the Commerce Commission's jurisdiction.

In December 2012 the Swiss Competition Commission fined Kühne + Nagel International AG CHF 1,173,767 for horizontal price-fixing of air freight fees and surcharges between 2003 and 2007. The case was closed by a negotiated settlement with the authority.

In July 2023 the Bundestag published a donation of €65,000 from Kühne to the CDU, received on 3 May 2023. Blick reported in June 2025 that he gave the CDU €65,000 to €70,000 a year in 2021 to 2023 and €70,000 in 2025, and at least €550,000 to German parties over 20 years, citing LobbyControl's analysis of Bundestag data.

In September 2026 Kühne+Nagel's chair said the company needed to address its Nazi-era past; the examination was expected to cover the expropriation of Jewish property, and its details and start date were not yet set. Bilanz reported that Kühne had opposed an in-depth study, notably one examining his father's role.

Euronews reported that after Kühne died on 24 August 2026 his fortune, including Kühne Holding's stakes in Kuehne+Nagel, Hapag-Lloyd and Lufthansa, passed to the Kühne Foundation. It noted that Schwyz is one of two Swiss cantons with no inheritance tax, and that Swiss law does not require private companies to publish annual reports.

politics.reason: Regular personal donations to Germany's CDU: the Bundestag published €65,000 received in May 2023; Blick reported €65,000 to €70,000 a year in 2021 to 2023, €70,000 in 2025, and at least €550,000 to German parties over 20 years, citing a LobbyControl analysis of Bundestag data. Blick found no registered Swiss political donations.

social.reason: Documented company-level competition problem: in the US, the EU, New Zealand and Switzerland, Kuehne + Nagel pleaded guilty, was fined or admitted taking part in cartels fixing air freight fees and surcharges, in conduct dating from 2002 to 2007. No specific labour or consumer finding was found.

legal.reason: Company-level record on air freight surcharge cartels (2002 to 2007): a US guilty plea with a $9.9 million fine (2011); a €53.7 million EU fine (2012), upheld by the EU courts in 2016 and 2018; a NZ$3.1 million penalty in New Zealand (2014); and a CHF 1.17 million Swiss fine in a settlement (2012). No personal legal record for Klaus-Michael Kühne was found.

unresolved.reason: According to Bilanz, Kühne opposed an in-depth study of the firm’s Nazi-era past during his lifetime. After his death in August 2026 the company said it needed to address it; in late September 2026 the study's details and start date were not yet set. His fortune passed to the Kühne Foundation; Swiss private companies need not publish annual reports.

proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 2: R5, a corporate guilty plea in a US federal court is a major company outcome, and the EU fine was upheld in contested appeals. Social 1 to 2: court-upheld cartel fines in four jurisdictions, as for L'Oréal. Politics stays 1: personal donations of about €70,000 a year are regular but modest for a major donor. Unresolved stays 2, re-sourced and updated. Ecology not researched. No counterweight: the foundation figures found were budgets, not amounts disbursed.

results.comment: Rewritten: DOJ plea agreement (Crim. No. 10-272, filed 4 Nov 2011) confirms entity, five 15 U.S.C. § 1 counts and $9,865,044 total fine; agreement signed September 2010 and court approval per Kuehne + Nagel release of 5 Nov 2011. Added the 2002 to 2007 conduct period (over ten years old) and 'fees and surcharges' (AAMS, NES, CAF, PSS).

Rewritten: removed 'the largest fine', which Logistics Manager does not state; added that the €169m was imposed on 14 forwarders. €53.7m (March 2012), General Court 2016 and Court of Justice February 2018 confirmed by the two sources.

Rewritten: the jurisdiction challenge was to the Commerce Commission's jurisdiction (lost in the High Court and Court of Appeal), not the court's; full entity name added. NZ$3.1m penalty plus costs, 8 April 2014, and admission confirmed by the Commerce Commission.

WEKO press release of 18 Dec 2012: decision of 11 Dec 2012, Kühne + Nagel International AG fined CHF 1,173,767 for horizontal price-fixing of fees and surcharges in 2003 to 2007, closed by amicable settlement (einvernehmliche Regelung).
